name: Velar Imperium
status_note: Status 'inactive' = no longer a functioning unified polity (controlled-vocabulary value). No longer exists as the unified galactic empire it once was. It is a failed/fractured state: its former core worlds were absorbed into the Galactic Union, and what remains persists only as post-imperial remnant territory held by splinter factions and remnant warlords.
government: A once-unified galactic empire that failed and fractured. No single authority commands it; what survives is contested among competing remnant factions: Imperial Loyalists (restorationists), Republican Reformists (constitutional reformers), and Outer Colony Warlords (frontier remnant strongmen). It is no longer a functioning empire — it is a post-imperial remnant.

successor_and_remnant_disposition.absorbed_into_galactic_union: A portion of the former Velar core was absorbed into the Galactic Union and now constitutes important Union core systems. Attested: Vel-Surak — a former Velar core world — is now bound to galactic_union and located in the Inner Mid-Disk Core Zone (loc_zone_inner_mid_disk_core).
successor_and_remnant_disposition.surviving_remnant: The remaining Imperium territory is the Velar Crescent (loc_zone_velar_crescent), the 'Post-Imperial Fault Line': ruin worlds (loc_velar_ruin_worlds), border worlds (loc_vel_border_01, loc_vel_core_01), and outer colony nodes (loc_velar_outer_colony_nodes) — the last held by the remnant Outer Colony Warlords.
successor_and_remnant_disposition.people_split: The Velari are split across both successors: species_velari.member_polities = [velar_imperium, galactic_union]. Membership in the Union does not extinguish Velari identity, and the remnant Imperium does not encompass the whole people.
successor_and_remnant_disposition.evidence: Derived from committed location records (loc_vel_surak → galactic_union / Inner Mid-Disk Core; the Crescent-bound Velar worlds → velar_imperium) and species_velari member_polities. Not invented.

traits: Deeply divided, vulnerable to external manipulation

promotion_pass: Filesystem Re-Sweep — Velar Imperium referent closure — 2026-07-21
notes: The Velar Imperium is a FAILED/FRACTURED former galactic empire — the origin polity of the Velari people — that no longer exists as the unified great power it once was. Its former core worlds were absorbed into the Galactic Union (e.g. Vel-Surak, now a Union core system in the Inner Mid-Disk Core Zone), while its surviving remnant is confined to the Velar Crescent (Post-Imperial Fault Line) and held by splinter factions and remnant warlords (Outer Colony Warlords). It was referenced across canon (species_velari origin_polity_id + member_polity, three internal-faction org records, the Union-Imperium border conflict, the virex_talvaren capsule, and multiple Velar location records) but had no parent entity record; this record closes that dangling canonical referent. Every attribute is recovered from the cited sources and cross-linked location/species records — not invented.

naming_exemption.reason: Polity name "Velar Imperium" preserved verbatim from GUMAS_Factions.json and the canonical timeline (Velar-Harkon Wars); the referent "velar_imperium" is already in canonical use across multiple committed records.

peoplehood_note: A STATE (a former imperial government, now fragmented), not the Velari people themselves. The Velari also hold membership in the Galactic Union (per species_velari.member_polities); the Imperium does not encompass the whole Velari people.
identity_model_note: Polity = a state / political entity, an orthogonal dimension from species (people), culture, and region. A polity does not describe a whole people.
certainty_basis: Existence is CANON (referenced by CANON species/location records and the timeline-attested Velar-Harkon Wars); attributes are recovered-source from the cited archive and cross-linked to existing internal-faction records. No invention.

history.basis: Reconciled 2026-08-09 from canon/L2/timeline/GUMAS_Galactic_Timeline_Detailed_Enhanced.json — the authoritative timeline. Surfaced by prose-claim salvage: early-project prose asserted the Imperium's arc (technocratic monarchy -> Celestial Surge -> Fracture War -> three-way split) and the check showed the timeline already held it while this entity record did not.
history.arc: Unification under a technocratic monarchy (Sahn'Darith Accord) -> peak expansion (Celestial Surge) -> collapse (Fracture War) -> fragmentation into the present three internal factions.

Sahn'Darith Accord.name: Sahn'Darith Accord
Sahn'Darith Accord.details: The Velari unified their star systems under a technocratic monarchy through the Sahn'Darith Accord, achieving peak cultural and technological development. This unification laid the groundwork for modern interstellar governance.

Celestial Surge.name: Celestial Surge
Celestial Surge.details: A technological renaissance featuring breakthroughs in terraforming, subspace navigation, and military innovation. The development of early Sentinel prototypes revitalized commerce and redefined military strategy across the galaxy.

Fracture War.name: Fracture War
Fracture War.details: Internal corruption, succession disputes, and external rebellions tore the Velar Imperium apart. The resulting Fracture War led to the emergence of distinct factions: Loyalist enclaves, Reformist movements, and Outer Colony Warlords.

history.fracture_outcome: The Fracture War produced the factions this record already carries: Imperial Loyalists (restorationists), Republican Reformists (Union-aligned constitutional reformers) and the Outer Colony Warlords (frontier strongmen).

social_structure.high_houses: Noble clans. Wield ancestral power, command legacy fleets, and hold ancient artifacts.
social_structure.margrave_orders: Military governors tasked with defending border systems. Some have gone rogue.
social_structure.lorekeepers_thessari: A monastic caste preserving pre-collapse history and genetic codices.
social_structure.citizen_tier: Citizen-Tier Velari are educated but politically voiceless unless granted "House Ascention" through merit or marriage.
social_structure.note: Describes the Imperium as a social order — it predates and outlives the unified state, which is why it is recorded on the polity rather than on any one faction.

naming_conventions.formal_style: First name + House/Lineage name (e.g. Sira Velkonn). Nobility or military rank precedes the name (e.g. Duchess Sira Velkonn, Commander Jaxx Tyren).
naming_conventions.informal_use: Close relations may drop the house name or use childhood honorifics (e.g. "Sira of Flamewake").
naming_conventions.corroboration: STRONG. The system was tested against Velari characters already committed to canon from independent sources and predicts their allegiances: Thalen Rynn (Rynn- = reformist) is "Voice of the Republican Reformist Assembly"; Jaxx Tyren (Ty- = outworld colonial/warlord) is "Warlord of the Outer Colonies"; Sira Velkonn, Talyx Velkonn and Syrr Velkonn (Vel- = noble) are respectively a pro-monarchy noble figure, an exiled Grand Duke and a Velar anthropologist. Canon was not written from this system, so the agreement is evidence the system is real rather than reconstructed.
naming_conventions.matching_caution: A prefix is a LINEAGE marker, not a substring test. Screening canon by substring also matched Mara Velthis (a Galactic Union captain, not Velar nobility) and Aveline Soryn — where "Vel" occurs inside the GIVEN name. Applying this system to identify houses requires the house/lineage element specifically.
naming_conventions.bearing: Relevant to the naming gate and NameService: it supplies a canonical basis for whether a newly discovered Velari name is plausible and which faction it implies. It does NOT license inventing names.

political_spectrum_note: The blueprint lists a FOURTH grouping beyond the three internal factions this record carries: "Neutral Houses" — hesitant or opportunistic factions watching for leverage or safety. No entity record exists; queued as velar-neutral-houses-referent. The blueprint's "Sim Status" column ("In development", "Awaiting generation", "candidate") is out-of-world production tracking, not in-world fact, and was not promoted.

marshal_council_corroboration.claim: Early prose: the conquest period "birthed the Marshal-Council System, from which Tal'Varen would later rise."
marshal_council_corroboration.status: CORROBORATION — no new canon. Canon already records the Marshal-Council System as born in the gravitic-drive conquest era (~300 years before present) and as the origin of the title "Lord Marshal" held by Virex Tal'Varen.
marshal_council_corroboration.note_worth_keeping: That same canon entry states the system is institutionally UNRELATED to the Union Marshals and that the shared word is coincidental — canon applying the same fragment-match discipline this salvage uses. Two "Marshal" institutions, explicitly declared distinct.
